deep.reconstruction:
This folio has no mathematics by Riemann. It is a printed bookseller's list. The header reads '1863. Catalog des Antiquarium's von W. Setzer in Bremen, Pelzerstraße Nr. 8', and the section is 'Mathematik', covering authors Thibaut to Vollmann (T–V). The page carries the stamp of the Turin bookseller Ermanno Loescher (Via Carlo Alberto 5) and a 'No. 1…' mark that is partly hidden by the stamp. A later archival hand has written '155 ↓ 162 = 8 Bl.' in pencil, meaning the catalogue fills folios 155–162, eight leaves, in the bundle.

The entries are bibliographic: author, short title, format (4 = quarto, 8 = octavo), place, year with the leading '1' dropped (so '824' means 1824), binding (Ppbd. = Pappband; Hlbfrzbd. = Halbfranzband; br. = broschiert; Ldrbd. = Lederband), and price in Silbergroschen (Sgr.) and Thaler. A figure in parentheses is the original publisher's price in Thaler.

There is no derivation, computation, or handwritten annotation by Riemann on the page, so nothing can be reconstructed mathematically.

Two listed items touch topics Riemann knew from Göttingen, but neither tells us anything about his own work:
- Vechtmann's 1843 Göttingen dissertation on lemniscates.
- Tralles on products with fixed sums of exponents, a partition-type extremal problem.

The catalogue being dated 1863 suggests it was filed among Riemann's papers late, or added by later custodians. That is a point of provenance, not of mathematics.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed 1863 antiquarian book catalogue (W. Setzer, Bremen; stamped by Ermanno Loescher, Turin). It contains no mathematics by Riemann, only a list of books for sale. It may be of minor interest for provenance or for reconstructing Riemann's library or reading, but it has no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: Price arithmetic for Thilo's 'Sammlung': 1 Thaler 10 Sgr equals 40 Silbergroschen, at 30 Sgr per Thaler (post-1821 Prussian currency).
Price arithmetic for Vega's 'Tafeln': 1 Thaler 25 Sgr equals 55 Sgr.

transcription_corrections: The currency sign rendered as '₰' (the Pfennig sign) is the printed Thaler abbreviation; it should be read as 'Thlr' (the next page's transcription uses 'Thlr'). So '1 ₰ 10 Sgr.' means 1 Thaler 10 Silbergroschen, and '(4 5/6 ₰)' means 4 5/6 Thaler.
The stamp reads 'LIBRAJO' with J for I (an old Italian spelling of 'Libraio'), as transcribed. 'No. 16' is uncertain: the number is partly covered by the stamp.
Uhlhorn entry: the image has 'Entdeckungen un der höh. Geometrie' (a printer's slip for 'in'). The transcription silently gives 'in'.
Vinhold entry: 'uuivers.' is the original printer's misprint for 'univers.'. It is not a transcription error.
Vechtmann entry: 'Leminiscatis' is as printed (a misprint for 'Lemniscatis'). A small ink mark near '843' in the image is not text.
Vlacq entry: 'tangent. and secant.' is as printed. Also note the publisher's price on the Uhde (1838) and similar entries is shown as fractions such as 22 1/2 Sgr, which is correctly transcribed.
